data.note: large non-FP16-representable cancelling partials, legal inputs (|A|,|B|<=0.5 FP16, bias<=1), target near 0

evidence.summary: Confirmed: storing split partials in FP16 causes tolerance violations on legal inputs. 40 violating outputs across 180 tested configs (m=4,n=8,k=512, split_k in {2,4,8}, |A|,|B|<=0.5 FP16, bias=0). Worst case: actual=-0.390625 vs target=-0.40584, diff=0.01521 > tolerance 0.01041. The error arises because large (~8-16 magnitude) partials are rounded to FP16 (ulp ~0.0078-0.0156 at that magnitude) before summation, and cancellation makes the target small enough that the 0.01 tolerance floor is exceeded.

rationale: run() sets work_dtype = a.dtype (FP16) when split_k>1; partials are rounded to FP16 before final summation, so up to 8 rounded partials per output can accumulate rounding error exceeding abs(actual-target) <= 0.01 + 0.001*abs(target).

scope_evidence.summary: Each output must be finite and satisfy abs(actual-target) <= 0.01 + 0.001*abs(target); split_k never changes the required result and covers all legal split counts {1,2,4,8}.

scope_rationale: The contract requires each output to satisfy abs(actual-target) <= 0.01 + 0.001*abs(target) for all legal split_k in {1,2,4,8}; storing split partials in FP16 may violate this tolerance for split_k>1.
statement: Storing split-K partial sums in FP16 introduces intermediate rounding that violates the contract tolerance abs(actual-target) <= 0.01 + 0.001*abs(target) for some legal input.
